messages:
alex: Seeing a sharp p95 east-west latency spike across GPU nodes during the 21:00-21:05 batching window. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/intersvc/plot/abc123
infra-alerts: Alert: inter-node p95 latency > 120ms for 3 consecutive batches on cluster-gpu-prod :rotating_light:
sam: Which racks/nodes are impacted? can you paste the node list?
alex: racks r5-r8, mostly gpu-r6-05..09 and gpu-r5-03..04. latency aligns with batch ramp at 21:00.
priya: Any recent NIC firmware, MTU or kernel changes rolled to those racks?
alex: No explicit MTU rollout, but I see repeated `rdma_cm` errors in dmesg on gpu-r6-07: `rdma_cm: route failed` and some RDMA connection retries.
maria: Can you run `tc -s qdisc show` and `ethtool -S` on one of the affected hosts? suspect qdisc drops under heavy burst.
ken: I pulled `ethtool -S gpu-r6-07` earlier: `tx_aborted_errors` incrementing, tx_dropped spikes during batch ramp.
sam: Could be jumbo frame mismatch. What are MTUs on source/dest?
alex: quick check: src gpu-r6-07 MTU=9000, gpu-r5-03 MTU=1500 for some of the older hosts — mixed MTU confirmed.
priya: That explains it. When batching increases, larger frames meet 1500 peers -> fragmentation/retransmits, RDMA fails back to TCP and latency spikes.
maria: Mitigation idea: avoid mixing older hosts in the hot-gpu pool during peak. Also temporarily reduce batch size/coalescing to reduce jumbo frame pressure.
ken: Suggest immediate mitigation: (1) set routing policy to avoid rack r6 for new batches; (2) reduce per-pod batch concurrency to 50% for the affected hostpool.
alex: Can we patch service routing? `rb route-set --policy avoid=r6 --scope batch-pool` (example). If someone from infra-oncall can do a quick canary.
infra-oncall: On it — applying a routing avoidance rule and halving batch concurrency for batch-pool. ETA ~8m. ping @sam @priya for rollback plan.
sam: Long-term: enforce MTU in provisioning images and add a boot-time check that fails hosts with non-9000 MTU for the GPU pool. Also schedule NIC firmware on r6-series; older Broadcom driver + coalescing mismatches seen before.
priya: Also add an RDMA health probe to node exporter (metric `rdma_cm_err_count`) and alert if >0 for N minutes. This will surface earlier than user-facing p95.
ken: Quick workaround patch applied: reduced batch size and set avoidance for r6. Results: p95 back down to ~18ms on affected flows.
alex: Confirmed — p95 dropped from ~140ms to ~18ms after the routing + batch throttle. Monitoring for 30m. Thanks :thumbsup:
infra-alerts: Auto-update: alert resolved at 1759502685.
alex: Follow-ups: run a full MTU inventory, plan a firmware window for r6, and add RDMA metric + grafana panel. I'll open tickets.
